name: gssdp
desc: GUPnP library for resource discovery and announcement over SSDP
why: SSDP is the discovery door behind UPnP, announcing devices on your LAN; a real look at how your router and gadgets find each other.

brief.what_it_is: gssdp is a GObject-based programming library for handling resource discovery and announcement over SSDP (Simple Service Discovery Protocol). Per the GitLab project page, it is an API, not a standalone command-line tool, so a program using it would announce its own devices or services on the network and search for others. The fetched pages do not describe the inputs and outputs in detail. Its GUPnP-family name suggests it sits beneath the UPnP stack.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as the GUPnP library for resource discovery and announcement over SSDP. The fetched pages give no further problem statement in the author's own words.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the package manager was visible in the fetched pages. The README I could reach was empty, so there are no build steps, dependencies, or first-run notes to report.
brief.standout: Instead of a finished app, it is a reusable GObject library, so other GNOME and GUPnP software can share one SSDP implementation. The scout note's framing of 'how your router and gadgets find each other' is a reasonable gloss on SSDP, but the fetched pages do not confirm it.
brief.status: Unknown for release activity. The GitLab project was created May 23, 2018, and the page showed no release date or last commit. The GNOME wiki homepage says the wiki is retired and points to handbook.gnome.org and gitlab.gnome.org for current information, so the project lives on GitLab.
brief.caveats: The listed homepage (wiki.gnome.org/GUPnP/) is a retired archive stub with no project content. The GitLab README at master/README.md loaded without its text, so the usage details here are thin. The only substantive description is one line from the GitLab project page. The license is GNU LGPLv2.1, as shown on GitLab. No commands, examples, or docs were available to verify.
